feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the positioning is clear, the experience progression is logical, and the content shows real scope across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. Impact is solid, but it would be stronger with more outcome-focused metrics, tighter formatting consistency, and less duplication across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative with strong specialization in enterprise web modernization, governance, and communications systems.  
- Good credibility through concrete scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms.  
- Writing is generally polished, professional, and aligned to senior-level digital strategy roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more results, not just responsibilities: include measurable outcomes such as traffic growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, cost savings, or adoption improvements.  
- Reduce repetition between Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT; consolidate to create a cleaner structure and more space for achievements.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation around lists is inconsistent; use either “social media and video” or “social, and multimedia” style consistently. Minor grammar/style issue: “launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production” is fine, but several bullets are long and could be tightened for readability. No obvious misspellings or major typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition plus 3–4 differentiators; reduce the long list of functions.
- Add one concrete scale marker from recent roles to increase impact (for example, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, or 50+ publishers).
- Replace “behind high-volume public-sector communications” with more direct, active phrasing.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance, analytics, and content operations for mission-driven public-sector organizations. Leads enterprise-scale digital transformation across CMS ecosystems, editorial workflows, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search and user experiences—most recently supporting a 10,000+ page Drupal platform serving 3.5M annual page views and 50+ internal publishers.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; consider narrowing this to “AI-enabled search.”
- The subtitle already signals leadership; avoid repeating broad labels like “digital leader” elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and with tighter, parallel wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure; e.g. “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting and insight infrastructure • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” or “user experiences” for clearer meaning.
- Standardize style: use either “and” throughout or “&” throughout; avoid mixing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider making it more capability-focused while leaving tools/platforms to later sections.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” in Topline Skills.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like an extension of the experience section and repeats several themes already covered there. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes, scope, or formats will make the footer feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use stronger, more specific verbs and cleaner lists: e.g., “Created an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”
- Standardize style and punctuation: use sentence case consistently; spell out “10-by-20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot” for CV consistency.
- Where possible, add one differentiator per project (audience, platform, scale, or purpose) to increase impact without adding much length.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the NACo consultant/director bullets.
- “Built/Developed” repeats across all four entries; vary verbs to avoid monotony.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo director role and Recent Projects. Make it sharper, more consultative, and outcome-oriented.

Suggested edit
- Reframe opening to emphasize advisory scope and seniority: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and web modernization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused lines, e.g.:
- “Designed and improved cross-channel digital systems, workflows, and analytics to support coordinated communications.”
- “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Provided CMS/front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for high-traffic public web properties.”
- “Led AI-enabled search planning, defining retrieval approach, structured content workflows, and discovery UX.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, reduced publishing time, or stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” and “enterprise web improvement” repeat the 2022–2024 director entry; keep this item focused on consulting/advisory and new initiatives.
- Microsite and AI-search details also appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same examples verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad first sentence with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and multi-channel communications.”
- Consolidate channel oversight into one impact-focused bullet and add metrics if available (email open/click rates, social growth, engagement, video output, budget/team size).
- Tighten bullets to action + result format, e.g. “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Consider a cleaner 5-bullet version: web migration; channel leadership; in-house studio build; analytics stack expansion; governance/operating model improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this one at a more strategic/enterprise level.
- Video-programming language overlaps with both the prior NACo role and Recent Projects; emphasize building the studio and organizational capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: operational scale, recurring programs, and cross-team systems.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting coordinated advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with systems language: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; use “managed” or “ran” instead of “led.”
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the prior role; frame this here as expansion/operationalization, not creation.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and public-sector relevance without repeating nearby phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad labels with sharper, executive-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations for high-volume publishing
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy, content planning & UX alignment
- Consider adding one qualifier tied to scale or complexity, e.g., “for complex, mission-driven organizations” if space allows.
- Keep wording parallel: all noun phrases, no mixed styles like “audience-focused” beside broader category labels.
- If you want more impact, swap the weakest line (“Audience-focused content planning”) for “Organizational content governance” or “Digital operating model design.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets; avoid repeating “communications operations” language exactly.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize highest-value, recent capabilities tied to enterprise web modernization and delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, with the strongest/recent items first.
- Cut lower-signal or older-feeling items unless central to target roles; keep this section scannable.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization
- Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)
- API integrations and workflow automation
- SharePoint and Power Pages
- Airtable-based content and operational systems
- AI-enabled search and discovery experiences
- If space allows, replace one platform name with an outcome-oriented phrase like “large-scale public-sector web delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let Technical + IT hold the full tool inventory.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; consider keeping it in only one place if space is tight.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the target roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize decision-making and optimization, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as outcomes + capabilities: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity for analytics infrastructure, dashboarding and user-behavior insights”
- Replace generic terms with sharper phrasing: change “Leadership reporting” to “executive dashboarding and decision support”
- Make optimization more specific: change “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, content performance and conversion analysis”
- Optional tighter version: “GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive reporting • SEO, content and conversion optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization” section; consider keeping tools there and using this line for higher-level capabilities.
- “KPI design” and “Leadership reporting” also echo recent NACo bullets; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and the broadcast/studio angle.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more specific, senior phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider swapping “Video production and editing” for “Broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect the in-house studio achievement.
- Drop one lower-signal item if space is tight; four items is cleaner than five.
- If you can support it elsewhere, align wording to outcomes: e.g., “in-house studio production” or “recurring advocacy video programming” rather than generic production terms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrase verbatim.
- “Studio operations” and “video production” are already evidenced in Director/Associate roles, so this section should summarize, not restate.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Since Drupal is central to the most recent roles, this item should emphasize depth and recency rather than read as a generic software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recentest platform: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Add light proficiency framing if space allows: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- If you want more impact, tie Drupal to scale: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Keep this item platform-only; leave implementation skills to the separate coding/technical section

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same tools plus CMS modernization
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor versus enterprise platforms unless it supports a project elsewhere

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic coding terms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from languages to applied capabilities: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they add little value and date the section.
- Consider replacing “Google Tag Manager” with “Tag management (Google Tag Manager)” to make it capability-led and clearer.
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context elsewhere on the CV, e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics instrumentation, and workflow automation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid repeating GitHub Actions if automation is covered more strongly in another item.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and reads like a generic software list. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills, so it should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to show intent, not just tools: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams”
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value/general collaboration tools (e.g., Slack, Teams) if space is tight; they add less differentiation for a senior digital leader.
- If accurate, strengthen with level cues: “Airtable (system design), Power Automate/Zapier (workflow automation), Jira/Asana (cross-team planning)”
- Keep ordering aligned to relevance/recency: lead with Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams may be redundant with general workplace fluency unless they were central to workflow design.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the level of ownership or scale shown elsewhere in the CV. It would be stronger if framed around enterprise email/engagement platforms rather than sounding like a generic tools inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize platform names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief: **Enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Keep it platform-focused only; let the work experience carry outcomes like newsletter reach and channel leadership

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated email-channel references in roles at NACo; avoid adding claims here like “managed newsletters reaching tens of thousands.”
- “Engagement” may blur with broader communications leadership already covered in Core Competencies; “Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms” is clearer and more specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” plus the Director role. Use it to sharpen the technical stack and optimization methods, not restate broader capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting**
- Replace vague **“Dashboarding”** with **“KPI reporting”** or **“executive dashboards”** for clearer business value.
- Consider swapping **SEO** for **Google Search Console** if you want this section to stay tool-focused; keep SEO in Topline Skills where it reads as a capability.
- If accurate, add one higher-signal method/tool only if used recently (e.g., **conversion analysis**, **funnel analysis**, or **tagging strategy**) instead of broad terms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This line closely overlaps with **Topline Skills [3]**; differentiate by making this item strictly tools/methods.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid adding descriptive claims here unless quantified elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is too general and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer outcomes if you can add them.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted through two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs/results where possible: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, or efficiency gains.
- Tighten the management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “supervised/mentored a digital media associate” only if it was a formal responsibility.
- Possible version: “Promoted through two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved multi-channel workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Mentored a digital media associate and helped expand in-house digital production capacity.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier buildout phase.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this lighter here.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities at NACo.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading its planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output metrics: number of episodes, audience, stakeholder groups served, or types of research/projects supported.
- Consider a stronger action/result framing: “Supported program and policy teams through research coordination and content development…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats themes covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Avoid overemphasizing general multimedia work here; save space for the first-podcast accomplishment, which is more distinctive.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps with stronger, more senior multimedia claims elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, and avoid repeating production capabilities already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
